sections.h2: What the Catawba County Register of Deeds records
sections.html:
The office records and keeps deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, powers of attorney, plats, easements, rights of way, assumed names and similar land documents. Birth and death records, marriage licenses and notary oaths are handled here too. The land records start in 1842, when the county was carved out of Lincoln County. Lincoln County keeps anything older.

Come between eight and five on a weekday, holidays excepted, to record a document or look at filed records. The phone number is (828) 465-1573. Indexes and images go online once a document is recorded, though they have not been verified. Recorded documents are scanned within one business day.

Voters elect the register. Staff are barred from preparing documents or answering legal questions, which means an attorney should draft the deed. Wills and divorces belong to the clerk of superior court at (828) 695-6100.

A paper filer delivers the signed, acknowledged deed with payment. An electronic filer goes through one of two eRecording companies: Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). The filer completes a memorandum of understanding with the company before the first submission. For 2023 the county counted 16,868 eRecorded real estate documents, a 74 percent average.

Paper filers should check a short list before the trip:

  • A deed cannot be accepted without the buyer's present mailing address on it.
  • A map or real estate instrument must name and address whoever receives it after recording.
  • Anything you want mailed back requires a stamped, addressed envelope big enough to hold it.
  • The instrument must meet the state's recording standards, and the office uses Times New Roman as its standard font.
  • A cover sheet may be required for some documents, so ask first if you are unsure.

Timing matters because of G.S. 47-18. A conveyance gives no protection against lien creditors or later buyers who paid value until it is registered where the land lies, and priority goes by the time of registration. Ask your closing attorney when the deed will reach the register.

Recording fees are set by state statute, and the county adds a few surcharges. The excise tax is separate, and the seller pays it.

Catawba County recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
General instruments, a deed among them$26.00 for pages 1 to 15, then $4.00 per added page
Loan security instruments (mortgage, deed of trust)$64.00 for pages 1 to 35, then $4.00 per added page
Subdivision plat$21.00 for every sheet
Paper that fails the state's format standards$25.00 extra
Assignment citing several deeds of trust$10 each after the first one cited
Instrument naming over 20 parties$2 for every extra party indexed
Photocopy of a recorded deed$.25 a page
Photocopy of a recorded plat$2.00 flat
Conveyance excise tax$1.00 per $500 of value, rounded up by fraction

Stated another way, the tax is $2.00 per $1,000 of price. The seller owes it, and a transfer for no payment needs no stamp. Satisfactions of deeds of trust record free. The counter takes cash, a business check, or a debit or credit card.

The county general fund keeps half of the excise tax, and the other half, less refunds and an allowance, goes to the state.

sections.h2: Looking up a property by address
sections.html:
The register's records describe land by legal description, not by street address, so an address search belongs with Tax Mapping. Three county numbers cover most seller questions:

  • Register of Deeds, (828) 465-1573, for recording, copies and the index.
  • Tax Mapping, (828) 465-8420, for matching an address to a parcel.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, (828) 695-6100, for wills and divorce records.

Mapping staff or the online real estate maps will do the address lookup. The GIS map is not a legal or binding map. Then take the parcel details to the Register of Deeds online deed search to read the chain of title.

The office cannot correct a missing item, error or misspelling on an original recorded document under G.S. 132-3, so expect to need an attorney for a correction. If a deed is lost, the office can issue a certified copy bearing its seal, which carries the same weight as the original.

The recording of a deed, more than the paper itself, is the main evidence of ownership. A seller who inherited or bought long ago should look for the vesting deed in the index before listing.

sections.h2: How recording ties to selling a house
sections.html:
With financing, a sale can produce three recordings: the deed to the buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, and a satisfaction of your old loan, which is free to record. Options, contracts to convey and leases over three years also need registration to bind later purchasers.

Chapter 47H governs contract-for-deed sales of one to four family homes in which the seller holds title through five or more payments. Within five business days the seller must record the contract or a memorandum of it, and the buyer can cancel through the third business day. A seller who used that structure should check the index for the memorandum.

On closing day the sequence is simple. The closing attorney confirms the buyer's mailing address, checks that the deed meets the recording standards and the excise tax is deducted from your proceeds. The deed then goes in by paper or through Simplifile or CSC, and it is scanned within one business day. After that the index shows the new owner, and the old loan's satisfaction, once recorded, clears your side of the chain. If something looks wrong on a recorded document, call the office first, then your attorney, since the register cannot correct the original.

Property tax runs alongside recording. What the parcel owes is stated by the tax office rather than the register, and a deferred circuit breaker balance comes due on transfer.

The county measures 413 square miles in the Blue Ridge foothills. The 2025 estimate is 170,172 people and 77,827 housing units. For 2020-2024 the median value of an owned home is $241,600, and 72.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

A seller who lives out of town can handle most of this by phone and mail, since the online indexes and the eRecording companies avoid a trip to the counter.

An old tract's chain of title can run back past 1842, and records before that year are held in Lincoln County.

faqs.q: Where is the Catawba County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8 to 5, holidays excepted. The phone is (828) 465-1573. Ask for the office's current street address when you call. eRecording is also available.

faqs.q: What are the charges for filing a deed with Catawba County?
faqs.a: The fee table above lists each charge. Page count drives the base fee, a $25.00 surcharge applies if the format rules are missed, and the seller separately owes the conveyance excise tax. Call (828) 465-1573 to confirm a total before you send a check.

faqs.q: Can Catawba County record a deed electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. All document types can be eRecorded through Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). The submitter completes a memorandum of understanding with the provider first.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds prepare deeds in Catawba County?
faqs.a: No. State law bars the office from preparing legal documents or giving legal advice, so you need an attorney to draft or correct a deed. Staff can show you the indexes, and certified copies of recorded deeds are $.25 per page.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Catawba County?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, pays the register before the deed is accepted. It is $1.00 per $500 of consideration, and a partial $500 counts as a whole one. Where nothing was exchanged, no stamp applies.
